text: Pedri can make an attack look simple because he makes the decision before everyone else has finished reading the picture. The pass into Raphinha against Feyenoord is the clearest example. At Valencia, there is another: Pedri combines with Dani Olmo and finishes the move himself. Creator, then runner. The roles change inside the same attack. Rodri also made his first Barcelona start in that Valencia game. In one sequence, his escape from pressure begins a combination through Fermin and Lamine, with Fermin eventually striking the post. That move did not even need to become a goal to explain the threat. Close down one player, and the ball can travel through another. The question for a pressing team is brutal: can you win it before Barcelona find the free man? If you cannot, the players you sent forward to press are now behind the action.
